title: The Face in the Feed
excerpt: A feed feels personal because it learns our habits. But recognition is not the same as being known, and a mirror can still be a machine.
content:
The strange intimacy of a feed is that it remembers without knowing us. It notices the pause before a video, the subject we return to, the hour when we are easiest to keep. Then it offers a version of the world shaped around those tiny admissions.

There is pleasure in being anticipated. A good recommendation feels like a friend handing us a book at exactly the right moment. But the feeling can hide a quiet substitution. The system is not asking what we love; it is measuring what keeps us there.

That difference matters because attention is not only a resource. It is how a life acquires texture. What we repeatedly look at becomes part of what seems normal, urgent, and possible. The feed does not need to control our opinions to change us. It only needs to decide which questions arrive often enough to feel like our own.

I still use the machines. The point is not purity. It is to leave a little unclaimed space in the day, enough to meet something that was not selected from the shape of yesterday’s self.
